VERDICT: EXTEND C0004 | FIND — `scan_health()` also misreports tool availability on tool timeout, not just missing binary. `_run_tool()` returns `CompletedProcess(..., returncode=-1, stderr="TIMEOUT")`, but each runner only special-cases `"NOT_FOUND"` and otherwise returns `[]`; `scan_health()` then sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` whenever the runner returns normally. FOLLOW — a hung pyright/ruff/bandit/mypy process is reported as available and healthy, so the insect brain cannot distinguish “tool ran and found nothing” from “tool never completed.” This silently suppresses health-scan degradation and can mislead round decisions exactly when infrastructure is unhealthy. FIX — when `_run_tool()` returns timeout/not-found sentinel status, propagate that status back to `scan_health()` and set `tools_available[tool_name] = False` for both cases.

VERDICT: MERGE C0001 <- F001 | FIND — same root cause as C0001/C0004: runner functions collapse execution failure into empty diagnostics, causing false availability reporting.

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox imports or multi-file context; it copies only the target file into a temp dir, then runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that isolated file path and optionally executes `test_cmd` in the temp dir without rewriting the command to point at sandboxed sources. Evidence: `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`; no other `source_paths` are copied. Post-fix analysis is `_count_tool_issues(..., patched_path)`. Test execution is `_run_tool(test_cmd, ..., cwd=tmpdir)`, but `test_cmd` is passed through unchanged.
FOLLOW: This breaks the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” capability in two ways. First, analysis of the patched file loses package/module context, so import/type errors caused by the fix can be missed or replaced by unrelated isolated-file diagnostics. Second, tests usually still run against the real repo tree if the command references original paths/modules, so verdicts can be marked SAFE/NEUTRAL even though the patched code was never exercised. That is a silently wrong result to the immune pipeline’s bug-closed gate: findings may be marked `verified=True` on the basis of a non-sandbox evaluation, causing NK dedup to close live bugs in later rounds.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — copy the full relevant source tree (at minimum all `source_paths`, preserving relative paths) into the temp dir, write the patched target into its mirrored location, and run tool/test commands against those sandboxed paths only.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify a fix as `SAFE` even when it introduces new errors in one tool, as long as the sum of net deltas across tools is not positive. Evidence: it computes `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues`; only `total_net > 0` is harmful. Example: `net_type_errors = +3`, `net_ruff_errors = -5`, `net_bandit_issues = 0` yields `total_net = -2` and verdict `SAFE`, despite three new type errors.
FOLLOW: This is silently wrong fix evaluation. A patch that breaks type checking or security but happens to reduce lint findings can be marked SAFE, then propagated by the immune pipeline as `verified=True`. Downstream, the bug-closed gate treats the issue as solved and suppresses future duplicate reports, so real regressions can be locked in.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — treat any positive per-tool delta (`net_type_errors > 0` or `net_ruff_errors > 0` or `net_bandit_issues > 0`) as `HARMFUL`; only classify as `SAFE` when no tool regresses and at least one metric improves or tests pass.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` records the wrong file in sandbox baselines because pre-fix counts are taken on the real file (`target_path`) while post-fix counts are taken on an isolated temp file (`patched_path`) with a different path/module context. This is not a like-for-like comparison. Evidence: `pre_* = _count_tool_issues(..., target_path)` before tempdir creation; `new_* = _count_tool_issues(..., patched_path)` after writing only the basename into tempdir.
FOLLOW: Even if the patch text is correct, net deltas can reflect path/context differences rather than the fix itself. For import-aware tools, moving a file out of its package can add or remove diagnostics unrelated to the change. The verdict engine then labels fixes SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL on a contaminated baseline, which feeds directly into immune verification and the verified-fix closure path.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — compute both pre-fix and post-fix diagnostics inside the same sandboxed file tree: copy sources to tempdir first, run baselines on the unmodified sandbox target, then patch that same sandbox file and rerun.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.40
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can select the wrong source file because it matches any extracted `*.py` token by substring containment: `if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. A short basename or partial path in a finding description/fix can match multiple entries, and the first hit wins.
FOLLOW: Fix evaluation can patch and analyze the wrong file while still returning a concrete verdict. That produces silently misleading SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL results, because the immune pipeline believes it evaluated the proposed fix for finding `finding_id` but actually tested another source file. Misverification can then mark the wrong bug as closed or leave the real one unevaluated.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — require unambiguous resolution: prefer exact normalized path match, then unique basename match; if multiple source paths match, return `None` and mark the fix `UNEVALUABLE` instead of choosing the first substring hit.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006
SEVERITY: 0.70
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_apply_fix_to_source()` accepts any syntactically valid Python text of 5+ lines as a whole-file replacement, even when the proposal is explanatory prose mixed with code or an unrelated snippet. Evidence: after `compile(fix, "<fix>", "exec")`, the only gate is `if fix.count("\n") >= 5: return fix`; there is no requirement that it correspond to the original file/module.
FOLLOW: The evaluator can “successfully” apply the wrong patch shape, replacing an entire file with arbitrary compilable text. Because verdicting is based on issue counts rather than semantic equivalence, this can produce false SAFE/NEUTRAL results for destructive replacements. Downstream, the immune pipeline may mark such a finding verified and close the bug on the basis of a non-root-cause patch.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — remove whole-file replacement fallback for PoC fix evaluation; only support explicit search/replace and line-level transformations that preserve the original file unless a structured patch format is added later.
VERIFIED: FALSE
